items.title: Open source license compliance generally available
items.summary: Enterprises can now manage their dependencies’ licenses at scale with sophisticated, ruleset-based checks that enforce a centralized policy. Open source license compliance is now generally available for GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers, including data-resident GHEC, for repositories with GitHub Code Security enabled. How it works Open source license compliance expands on the capabilities of the dependency review action by introducing an enterprise-wide license policy. items.title: Xcode 27 runner image generally available
items.summary: You can now use the generally available Xcode 27 runner image to build and test your Apple applications in GitHub Actions. Previously in public preview, this GitHub-hosted image runs on macOS 27 and includes the Xcode 27 toolchain and Apple SDKs. Xcode-based images Each image supports one major Xcode version rather than targeting a specific operating system version. This makes it easier to select the toolchain your project needs and know what each runner provides. items.title: Multi-repository support and other improvements for GitHub in Slack and Teams
items.summary: @GitHub in Slack and Teams now supports working across multiple repositories in a single conversation. Whether you’re creating issues, opening pull requests, or investigating bugs, you can work across repositories without switching conversations. For example, you can ask @GitHub to: Create issues from conversations: “@GitHub Create an issue in github/issues to track this bug, using the context from this thread.” Make code changes: “@GitHub Fix this bug in our frontend repository and open a PR with the changes.” Track your PRs: “@GitHub Show me all my open PRs across repositories and...

items.title: Download GitHub Code Quality license usage as a CSV
items.summary: You can now download a CSV report of your GitHub Code Quality license usage to reconcile your license count with your own records. The report includes: Each active committer who consumes a Code Quality license. The repositories that received their commits in the last 90 days. Whether each committer is unique to a single repository or organization. Use the unique committer details to identify where disabling Code Quality could free up licenses for the next billing period without changing your current license charge. items.title: AI Scan for pull requests generally available
items.summary: Code scanning AI Scan for pull requests is now generally available. It complements CodeQL by finding vulnerabilities in pull request changes for languages and frameworks that CodeQL does not currently cover, including PHP, Shell/Bash, Terraform configuration (HCL), Dockerfiles, JSP for Java, Blazor for C#, and more. How it works AI Scan runs automatically on pull requests when code scanning and the repository’s effective AI Scan setting are enabled. Findings appear alongside CodeQL results on the Conversation and Files changed tabs, with an “AI” indicator to distinguish them from CodeQL...

items.title: Agentic autofix for code scanning alerts general availability
items.summary: Agentic autofix for code scanning alerts is now generally available. It remediates alerts by working across your codebase the way a developer would: it explores relevant files, proposes a fix, and reruns CodeQL to confirm the fix closes the alert before opening a pull request for your review. Agentic autofix is available to GitHub Code Security and GitHub Advanced Security customers on GitHub Enterprise Cloud, including GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency. items.title: Email notifications for repository push events have been retired
items.summary: As of October 15, 2026, email notifications for repository push events have been retired and are no longer sent. We shut down this feature to help prevent spam and abuse. Because recipients didn’t have to consent before receiving these emails, the feature could be misused to send unwanted messages through GitHub’s email infrastructure. To continue sending email notifications for repository push events, you can use a GitHub Actions workflow triggered by push events to send emails through your own SMTP server or email provider. items.title: HydraFusion updates and new Max option
items.summary: HydraFusion has an updated model pool, improved orchestration workflows, and introduces HydraFusion Max. Both HydraFusion and HydraFusion Max are available across VS Code, the GitHub Copilot app, and GitHub Copilot CLI and remain in research preview. HydraFusion orchestrates multiple models to produce a single response, bringing together their strengths so you don’t have to choose an individual model for each task. What’s new in HydraFusion Latest frontier models: HydraFusion and HydraFusion Max draw from a pool that now includes Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, and GPT-6 Luna....

items.title: GitHub Actions workflow lockfiles in public preview
items.summary: GitHub Actions workflow dependency lockfiles are now in public preview for GitHub Enterprise Cloud, GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency, Team, and Free plans. Tags and branches can move after you review a workflow, so a later run might execute different code. Lockfiles let you keep those references in your workflow while running the exact commits you locked. Editor’s note (October 14th, 2026): Updated which plans have access to this public preview.
